subject: Privacy clause consolidation and signer pathway for ZenHealth DPA

Date: Tue, 01 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: ZenHealth DPA — initial redlines and questions

Hi Grace,

Thanks for the demo last week — excited to move forward. Attached are our initial DPA redlines (track changes) and a short list of clarifying questions:

- Can you confirm whether Redwood will be relying on standard EU SCCs or a custom transfer mechanism?
- Retention: we asked for a 2-year maximum for derivatives — please confirm your stance.
- HIPAA: we need confirmation that Redwood will sign a BAA for PHI as a processor for the pilot.
- Evidence: please provide SOC 2 Type II report (most recent) and SIG responses for security review.

We also need to understand the signing authority (who at Redwood will execute) and whether you use DocuSign for counterparty signatures. Procurement would like an estimated timeline to finalize.

Attachments: zen_dpa_redlines.docx

Thanks — if we can get legal review this week that would be great.

Sana

Subject: Re: ZenHealth DPA — initial redlines and questions

Hi Sana — thanks for the redlines and the clear list. We'll run these through legal and security immediately. Quick answers up front:

- SCCs: we accept incorporation of the Standard EU SCCs (we can insert the module language) — Marcus/Neha will confirm final wording.
- Retention: will flag for Legal; we typically look to align on a service-driven retention cap and can propose a 24-month cap for derived analytics if that meets your risk threshold.
- HIPAA/BAA: Redwood can sign a BAA for the pilot; technical controls and evidence will be documented.
- Evidence: SOC 2 Type II and our SIG (completed) will be shared via a secure Drive link.

Proposed next steps (MAP):
1) Redwood legal to produce a counter DPA with tracked changes (within 48 business hours).
2) Security to upload SOC2 + SIG pack to secure Drive (same day).
3) Align on signers and route (DocuSign recommended) — please confirm ZenHealth signers.

I'll loop in Marcus and Neha for legal language and signoff.

Best,
Grace O'Connor
Head of Customer Partnerships | Redwood Inference

Grace — attaching a cleaned PDF of our redlines with comments. A few clarifications from Legal:

- We need explicit confirmation that Redwood will incorporate Module Two (Controller-to-Processor) SCCs for EU data flows.
- Section 7 (Retention): ZenHealth requires a max 24 months for derivatives and deletion/return obligations for primary PHI datasets unless otherwise consented.
- Subprocessors: require 30-day notice for new subprocessors in production.

Signer authority at ZenHealth will be: CFO (financial terms) and CISO (security appendix). If Redwood requires a different signer mix, let us know.

Attachment: Zen_DPA_redline_track_changes.pdf

Marcus / Neha — forwarding ZenHealth's cleaned redline and notes above. Key asks: EU Module Two SCCs, 24-month derivatives retention, 30-day subprocessor notice, and BAA for PHI. They plan to have CFO + CISO sign.

Questions for Legal:
- Which redlines do we accept versus push back on? I think the 24-month derivatives cap is reasonable for the pilot, but subprocessor notice at 30 days might be tight — can we propose 45 days?

- Any material exposure in their proposed breach notification language?

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 03 Jun 2027 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: ZenHealth DPA — cleaned redline + signer authority

Thanks Grace — reviewed. Proposed legal position (high level):

1) Retention: agree to 24 months for derived analytics; we will limit primary dataset retention to contractually agreed retention schedules and will offer data deletion on contract termination.
2) SCCs: accept Module Two inclusion. We'll add a narrow carveout for telemetry logs (operational telemetry retained for 90 days unless required for investigations).
3) Subprocessors: counter to 45-day notice for new subprocessors; for critical infra changes we can give 30 days.
4) HIPAA/BAA: we will sign a BAA for the pilot. Security must confirm the list of technical controls (encryption at rest/in transit, access controls).
5) Breach notifications: accept 72-hour initial notification to ZenHealth security for incidents involving PHI.

I drafted a counter with tracked changes — attached: redwood_counter_dpa_v1.docx. Please route this to Security to attach SOC2 + SIG, then I'll prepare a short risk memo for exec signer approval.

Neha Kapoor
Senior Counsel | Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwood.com
